native_review.summary: The conversation proceeded successfully. The agent authenticated the user via name + zip code after the email lookup failed, reasonably denied the split-payment request, provided the required information about the most expensive item (Action Camera at $481.50), and correctly handled the request to switch all items to the cheapest available same-product variants. The agent itemized the modification plan, obtained explicit user confirmation including all items and the refund payment method, and executed modify_pending_order_items, bringing the total to $1130.85 with a $36.13 refund. The only error was a minor policy violation in TURN 18 where the agent made multiple tool calls at once and responded to the user in the same turn; this did not affect the outcome. No user simulator errors were found.

errors.reasoning: The agent sent a message to the user and simultaneously made five get_product_details tool calls in a single turn. This violates the policy rule that the agent should make at most one tool call at a time and should not respond to the user while making a tool call (and vice versa). The violation did not affect the final outcome since all the lookups were relevant and correct.
errors.correct_behavior: The agent should have made the get_product_details calls one at a time (one tool call per turn) and should not have included a user-facing message in the same turn as the tool calls.

auth_classification.reasoning: The initial authentication attempt using email failed, but the agent subsequently verified the user's identity via name and zip code lookup, which successfully returned the user's account. Therefore, the user was eventually authenticated.
